papers.title: Optimal odd unimodular lattices in dimensions $49$ through $59$
papers.abstract: It is shown that the largest minimum norm among unimodular lattices is $4$ in dimension $49$ and $5$ in dimensions $50$, $51$, $57$ and $58$. We also study the theta series of optimal unimodular lattices in every dimension from $49$ through $59$. In dimensions $50$, $51$ and $57$, the first known examples of unimodular lattices with minimum norm $5$ are obtained from self-dual codes by Construction~A. There exist at least $25$, $2$, $3$, $7$ and $12$ nonisomorphic optimal unimodular lattices in dimensions $49$, $55$, $57$, $58$ and $59$, respectively.

papers.title: On the tensor product of semistable Hermitian adelic vector bundles over an adelic curve
papers.abstract: We prove tensor semistability for Hermitian adelic vector bundles on proper adelic curves whose underlying fields are countable and of characteristic zero. The central estimate concerns the canonical integral Specht lattice of a rectangular partition with fixed height: its logarithmic covolume, divided by its rank and tensor degree, tends to zero. We prove this estimate from monic seminormal norms and an exact hypergeometric law weighted by the square of a Vandermonde product for tableau prefixes. Constant adelic Specht bundles and equivariant contractions then yield the slope inequality for every geometrically semistable subspace of a finite tensor product. The correction is the measure of the Archimedean places times a sublinear Specht term and vanishes in the limit as the auxiliary degree tends to infinity. An instability-filtration argument completes the reduction to arbitrary factors and identifies the tensor product Harder--Narasimhan filtration. The number field specialization gives the Bost tensor semistability conjecture in all ranks.

papers.title: The local lifting conjecture for dihedral groups of order $2p^n$
papers.abstract: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of odd characteristic $p$, and let $D_{p^n}$ denote the dihedral group of order $2p^n$. A local $D_{p^n}$-action is a faithful action of $D_{p^n}$ on the formal power series ring $k[[z]]$ by continuous $k$-automorphisms. The strong Oort conjecture of Chinburg, Guralnick and Harbater predicts that every such action lifts to characteristic zero. This is also the dihedral case of the local lifting conjecture of Obus. We prove this assertion for $n=2$ and every odd prime $p$. More precisely, given a local $D_{p^2}$-action on $k[[z]]$, we construct an action on $R[[Z]]$ by $R$-automorphisms whose reduction modulo the maximal ideal of $R$ is the given action, where $R$ is a complete discrete valuation ring finite over the Witt ring $W(k)$. For arbitrary $n$, let $C_{p^n}$ be the cyclic subgroup of index two in $D_{p^n}$, and let $u_1,\ldots,u_n$ be the upper ramification jumps of $k((z))/k((z))^{C_{p^n}}$. We prove that the action lifts if $u_i\equiv-1\pmod{2p}$ for every $i$. When $p=3$, we also prove lifting under the hypotheses $u_i\equiv5\pmod6$ for $2\leq i<n$ and $3\nmid u_n$.

papers.title: Grothendieck--Serre for quasi-split groups over two-dimensional regular local rings
papers.abstract: We prove the Grothendieck--Serre conjecture for quasi-split reductive group schemes over two-dimensional regular local rings, that is, every generically trivial torsor under a quasi-split group scheme $G$ over a regular local ring $R$ of dimension two is trivial. Our main result is new when $R$ is ramified and generalizes Nisnevich's result by removing the assumption that the residue field is infinite. By formal patching of torsors and valuative criteria, we are reduced to showing a product formula when $G$ is semisimple and simply connected. Then, we take advantage of relative simple reflections and relative Bruhat decomposition to prove a generation by rank-one subgroups. The analysis on Dynkin diagrams with Galois actions reduces us to $\operatorname{SL}_2$ and three-dimensional $\operatorname{SU}$ factors. For the special unitary case, we treat Hermitian forms by using stabilizations and cancellation to finish the proof.

papers.title: Rank-Two Attractors and Modularity for a Mirror Bicubic
papers.abstract: We study the mirror family $\mathcal X_\lambda$ of the bicubic Calabi-Yau threefold, obtained from a family of complete intersections of two cubics in $\mathbb P^5$. We show that the four-dimensional weight-three Hodge structure of the fibers over $\lambda^6 = -8$ splits into two rational rank-two pieces of Hodge types $(1,0,0,1)$ and $(0,1,1,0)$; in particular, these points are rank-two attractor points. Using a Hesse pencil fiber-product realization, equivariant point counting, and the Serre-Faltings-Livne method, we identify their semisimplified $\ell$-adic Galois representations with those attached to the weight-four newform $f_{\mathsf{54.4.a.c}}$ and the Tate twist of the weight-two newform $f_{\mathsf{54.2.a.a}}$, where these labels refer to the L-functions and modular forms database.

papers.title: The Tate conjecture for abelian fourfolds
papers.abstract: We prove the Tate conjecture for non-CM and non-ordinary abelian fourfolds over positive characteristic function fields. Combining our previous works (2512.00687 and 2608.28651), this establishes the Tate conjecture for abelian fourfolds over finitely generated fields. Along the way, we classify the $l$-adic monodromy of abelian fourfolds in characteristic $p$ via mixed characteristic lifts and methods from convergent and overconvergent crystalline monodromy, and show that Zarhin's minuscule weights conjecture holds for abelian varieties up to dimension 4. These enable us to prove a characteristic $p$ variant of the Mumford--Tate conjecture for most abelian fourfolds, and reduce the Tate conjecture to Markman's results on the Hodge conjecture.

papers.title: Quasi-abelian Cousin groups of number fields:a Galois-orbit criterion and the complete list
papers.abstract: Let K be a number field with at least one complex place. A choice S of one embedding K $\rightarrow$ C at each place embeds the ring of integers of K as a discrete subgroup of Cn, where n is the number of places of K. The quotient T\_K,S is a Cousin group, or a complex torus if K is totally imaginary. We determine exactly when T\_K,S is quasi-abelian. The answer is a Galois criterion: no complex conjugation of the Galois closure of K may interchange two of the chosen complex embeddings. Equivalently, S is lifted from a subfield with at most one complex place above each place of the largest totally real subfield of K. For totally imaginary K this is the theorem of Shimura and Taniyama on abelian varieties with complex multiplication; our results extend it to all number fields. We also obtain the rank of the N{\'e}ron--Severi group, and show that T\_K,S is either quasi-abelian or has only constant meromorphic functions.

papers.title: Degree three unramified cohomology of homogeneous spaces with finite stabilisers
papers.abstract: We provide an explicit formula for the third unramified cohomology group of homogeneous spaces of $\mathrm{SL}_n$ with finite stabilisers and a rational point, valid over an arbitrary field of characteristic prime to the order of the stabilisers. As a concrete application, we compute this group explicitly for every generalised quaternion group over an arbitrary field of characteristic 0, and settle Noether's problem over the rational numbers in the negative for those of order at least 16, thereby generalising a classical result of Serre. Over an algebraically closed field, our formula recovers and sharpens a theorem of Peyre; we further show that universal triviality of unramified cohomology in degree at most three is equivalent to its vanishing in the same degrees. Over the function field of a $p$-adic curve, we extend a result of Harari-Scheiderer-Szamuely. Over a finite field, the formula is effective and yields an algorithm for computing the group explicitly.

papers.title: $\mathbb{Q}_p$-analytic intersections of $\mathbb{C}_p$-analytic manifolds with perfectoid Banach--Colmez spaces
papers.abstract: We show that transverse intersections between smooth $\mathbb{C}_p$-analytic manifolds in $\mathbb{C}_p^n$ and perfectoid Banach--Colmez spaces of complementary $\mathbb{C}_p$-dimension are $n$-dimensional $\mathbb{Q}_p$-analytic manifolds. In the case of the Banach--Colmez space $\mathrm{BC}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)$, this is a strong form of the relativistic $p$-adic sunscreen conjecture. These results hold more generally with $\mathbb{C}_p$ replaced by an arbitrary complete algebraically closed extension of $\mathbb{Q}_p$, and we also establish some non-linear analogs for infinite level Lubin--Tate spaces.

papers.title: Explicit Error Term in the Chebotarev Density Theorem for Function Fields
papers.abstract: We prove an explicit error term in the Chebotarev Density Theorem for finite generically Galois \'etale morphisms of affine varieties over finite fields, under a mild condition on their size. The error term generalises the known results for curves, and depends only on invariants of the varieties. We present several applications to the explicit error term. We apply it to existence problems, and to the Bateman-Horn conjecture over finite fields.

papers.title: The Tate Conjecture in Positive Characteristic
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{Z}(n)$ be Bloch's cycle complex and $\mathbb{Z}(n)^c$ be the complex that compute continuous \'etale cohomology. Kahn observed that the Tate conjecture for a finite field is equivalent to the map $\mathcal{Z}(n)\otimes\mathbb{Z}(0)^c\to\mathbb{Z}(n)^c$ being isomorphism. Later, Kahn found that the Tate conjecture for a finite field is equivalent to $\Omega_\ell(\mathbb{Z}_\ell)\in DM^{\text{eff}}_{\text{\'et}}(k)$, where $\Omega_\ell$ is the right adjoint of the $\ell$-adic realisation functor. In this note, using the Dwyer-Greenlees equivalence between $\ell$-completed objects and $\ell$-torsion objects, we prove that $\Omega_\ell(\mathbb{Z}_\ell)\in DM^{\text{eff}}_{\text{\'et}}(k)$, and consequently, based on Kahn's early work, the Tate conjecture at positive characteristics.

papers.title: Reduction types of curves in tame extensions
papers.abstract: Let $C/K$ be a curve of genus $g\geq 1$ over a discretely valued field $K$ with algebraically closed residue field. In this paper, we study the behaviour of the reduction type of $C$ under finite tame extensions. If $L/K$ is a tame extension of degree $n$, we give sufficient conditions on the reduction type $R$ of $C$ so that the reduction type of the base change $C_L$ is uniquely determined by $R$ and $n$. In particular, if $C$ has abelian and toric ranks zero, then $R$ satisfies these conditions. We also give an algorithm to compute the possibilities for the reduction type of $C_L$ given only $R$ and $n$. The main method involves studying harmonic covers of graphs with a cyclic action. As a result, we obtain a characterisation of tame curves with potentially good reduction in terms of their reduction type, and a new proof of a result by Liu-Lorenzini-Raynaud regarding the non-realisability of certain reduction types.

papers.title: Kato-Milne cohomology over rational function fields in characteristic p>0
papers.abstract: Let F be a field of characteristic p > 0. In this note, we describe the Kato-Milne cohomology of the rational function field F(x) in one variable x over F. In particular, we extend the Milnor-Scharlau exact sequence [12, Theorem 5.2] to characteristic p. As an application of this exact sequence, we further obtain the norm theorem [16, Theorem A.3] in characteristic p.

papers.title: The Riemann Hypothesis for L-Functions of Linearly Constrained Kloosterman Families: Frobenius Polynomials and Intersection Cohomology
papers.abstract: We study Frobenius polynomials attached to linearly constrained Kloosterman families, taking the rank-$r(n)=2^n-\binom{n}{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}$, weight-$(n+1)$ sheaf of the author's companion papers as an explicit input. The present contribution is the passage from that sheaf to local characteristic polynomials and the intermediate-extension intersection cohomology on $(\mathbb P^1)^n$. We prove the local reciprocal-root bounds and the degreewise purity of the completed factors; their weights are $n+1+i$ in cohomological degree $i$. Using the imported arithmetic relative-image identification, we construct a reflection pairing and derive the completed functional equation with positive root number. We also give a canonical Frobenius-equivariant splitting of the fibrewise compact-support/parabolic sequence by separation of weights and examine the comparison on open coordinate-zero divisors. The statements do not assume global arithmetic Frobenius semisimplicity or a higher-codimension wild-boundary exchange. An explicit source-and-dependency ledger distinguishes results imported from the companion papers from deductions established here.

papers.title: Connected descent and Brauer-Manin set for 0-cycles
papers.abstract: We answer a question by Hui Zhang and show that, for any smooth, quasi-projective, geometrically integral variety X over a number field k, the connected descent set for 0-cycles is equal to the Brauer-Manin set for 0-cycles. In particular, the connected descent and the abelianised connected descent sets for 0-cycles coincide. In the same spirit, we also show that the descent set under all tori for 0-cycles is equal to the algebraic Brauer-Manin set for 0-cycles. Finally, we give a new formulation of Conjecture (E) using the connected descent sets.

papers.title: On the work of Jacob Tsimerman
papers.abstract: Jacob Tsimerman was awarded a Fields Medal at the\ ICM in Philadelphia on July 23, 2026 ``For his contribution in the recasting of o-minimality as a fundamental method of arithmetic and complex algebraic geometry, and his role in the proof of many central conjectures including Griffiths' conjecture on the algebraicity of images of the period maps, and the Andr\'e-Oort conjecture for Siegel modular varieties.'' We describe this work.

papers.title: Arithmetic Winding Curves in $\mathbb{F}_1$ Geometry
papers.abstract: We construct arithmetic winding curves from cyclic covers and the completions of a number field $K$. Transfers between cyclic periods give the primitive cyclotomic relations. Selected factors of the equivariant endomorphism rings of their derived intersections are finite fields in odd residue characteristic and length-two Witt rings in residue characteristic two. Valuation covers carry these periods on the curve $Y_K$. Their normal coordinates realize deck shifts as Schwartz operators in Meyer's arithmetic trace formula, and their puncture differentials give the finite Euler factors of $\zeta_K$. We construct a sheaf on $Y_K$ for which the middle Fourier--Poisson representation embeds as a $C_K$-module in ordinary first sheaf cohomology. The Dedekind-zeta component is an equivariant direct summand. The injection uses valuation monodromy at the finite places and adelic Poisson summation on the archimedean charts. The cup product of two image classes vanishes with tensor-product coefficients, also after conjugating one factor. On the section side, tensor degree and integral jets give multiplicative lattices, explicit duality quotients, and relative theta identities. A principal cyclotomic twist with determinant one on truncated jets yields a quadratic lower bound for the logarithmic index in a family of increasing rank. The fixed-weight Poisson quotients preserve finite collections of Mellin derivatives at Hecke zeros of orders below their respective multiplicities.

papers.title: Notes on an elementary proof of Weil II from Hexagon
papers.abstract: Recently, L. Alp\"oge sketched an elementary proof of Deligne's weight bound in footnote 3 of his remark on joint work with Claude on the Riemann hypothesis. An expanded, AI-generated account appeared on Hexagon, where it was posted by F. Alderliefste. This note gives an exposition of the proof presented there.

papers.title: Hypergeometric Abelian Surfaces and Triangle-Group Levels
papers.abstract: We study three families of hypergeometric abelian surfaces with real multiplication by $K=\Q(\sqrt5)$. We determine their integral homology lattices and monodromy, including the choice of lattice at the ramified prime above $5$ in the plus family. One family is isomorphic to an explicit quadratic twist of a genus-two Frey Jacobian, with the two real-multiplication embeddings exchanged. The specified isogeny is twice an isomorphism and has kernel equal to the full $2$-torsion. Each family gives two real rank-two representations, with projective local monodromies of order $5$ at two punctures and parabolic monodromy at the third. Exactly one of the six projective representations is discrete, with image $\Delta(5,5,\infty)$. Reduction at the two primes above $11$ gives six degree-$12$, genus-two covers parametrizing torsion lines. For the family with a discrete constituent, these Borel covers are the triangular modular curves $X_0(5,5,\infty;\mathfrak q)$; the comparison descends to ordered covers over $K$. The generic arithmetic projective image is $\PGL_2(\F_{11})$; the Galois closure of each Borel cover has constant field $K(\sqrt{-11})$.

papers.title: Three commuting matrices whose lifts never commute
papers.abstract: We construct pairwise commuting matrices over $\mathbb{F}_p$ which have no pairwise commuting lifts to $\mathbb{Z}/p^2\mathbb{Z}$. Equivalently, there are mod $p$ representations of the absolute Galois group of the field of iterated Laurent series $\mathbb{C}((x_1))\cdots((x_d))$ which do not lift modulo $p^2$.

papers.title: On Some Diophantine Parameters of the Cyclic Torsion Subgroups of Odd Order of Elliptic Curves over $\mathbb{Q}$
papers.abstract: For elliptic curves $ E $ over the rational number field $ \Q, $ based on Mazur's classical result, we give in this paper some explicit Diophantine parameters for their cyclic torsion subgroups $ E(\Q)_{\text{tors}} $ of odd order. This work is a continuation of the ones in ([Q1], [QZ1$\sim $2]). Such explicit form of parameters might be useful in calculating torsion subgroups of elliptic curves over higher degree number fields.

papers.title: Differential forms and Brauer classes in positive characteristic
papers.abstract: We study $p$-torsion Brauer classes in positive characteristic arising from differential forms. We relate this construction to the Brauer group of supersingular K3 surfaces and analyze the contribution of these classes to the Brauer-Manin obstruction. As an application, we examine the Brauer-Manin set of supersingular K3 surfaces and of varieties admitting many differential forms.

papers.title: Classification of torsion of elliptic curves over quartic fields
papers.abstract: Let $E$ be an elliptic curve over a quartic field $K$. By the Mordell-Weil theorem, $E(K)$ is a finitely generated group. We determine all the possibilities for the torsion group $E(K)_{tor}$ where $K$ ranges over all quartic fields $K$ and $E$ ranges over all elliptic curves over $K$. We show that there are no sporadic torsion groups, or in other words, that all torsion groups either do not appear or they appear for infinitely many non-isomorphic elliptic curves $E$. Proving this requires showing that numerous modular curves $X_1(m,n)$ have no non-cuspidal degree $4$ points. We deal with almost all the curves using one of 3 methods: a method for the rank 0 cases requiring no computation; the Hecke sieve, a local method requiring computer-assisted computations; and the global method, an argument for the positive rank cases also requiring no computation. We deal with the handful of remaining cases using ad hoc methods.

papers.title: Genus and Gonality of Small Curves, Dynamical Uniform Boundedness, and Bifurcation
papers.abstract: We prove that a complex one-parameter algebraic family of endomorphisms of $\mathbb{P}^N$ has a non-empty bifurcation set if and only if the genus grows superlinearly in degree along every generic sequence of dynatomic curves. In this case, gonality also tends to infinity. In particular, for non-isotrivial families on $\mathbb{P}^1$, gonality tends to infinity along distinct dynatomic curves, while superlinear genus growth holds for every such sequence exactly when the family is not a flexible Latt\`es family. We also establish analogous results for generic sequences of small curves. As applications, we prove uniform boundedness results for iterated preimages over number fields and geometric uniform boundedness results for preperiodic points over function fields. The proof combines arithmetic equidistribution, woven currents, and bifurcation theory. The bifurcation mechanism is what forces the growth of genus and gonality.

papers.title: Upper Bounds on the de Bruijn-Newman constant for Dirichlet $L$-functions with primitive real-valued characters
papers.abstract: Let $\chi_m$ be a primitive real-valued Dirichlet character of conductor $m\ge3$, let $L(s)=L(s,\chi_m)$ be the associated Dirichlet $L$-function, and let $\xi_L(s)$ denote its completed form. For each $t \in \mathbb R$, we define the entire function \[ H^L_t(z) := \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} e^{tu^2} \Phi_L(u) e^{izu} du, \] where $\Phi_L$ is the superexponentially decaying density \[ \Phi_L(u) := \frac{1}{2\pi}\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} \xi_L \left(\frac{1+is}{2}\right) e^{-isu} ds. \] The family $\{H_t^L\}_{t \in \mathbb R}$ describes the heat-flow evolution of $\xi_L$ and solves a backward heat equation. By the work of Newman, there exists a finite constant $\Lambda_L$, called the generalized de Bruijn--Newman constant, such that all the zeros of $H_t^L$ are real if and only if $t \ge \Lambda_L$. The Generalized Riemann Hypothesis for $L$ is equivalent to the assertion that $\Lambda_L \le 0$. Dobner established the matching lower bound $\Lambda_L \ge 0$, while de Bruijn proved the upper bound $\Lambda_L \le \tfrac12$. We prove the unconditional uniform bound $\Lambda_L\le95241/320000=0.297628125$ for every primitive real-valued character of conductor $3\le m\le400$, together with stronger individual bounds. The proof extends the effective approximation of Polymath to Dirichlet $L$-functions, retaining the conductor dependence in the error estimates. We combine these estimates with Platt's numerical verification of GRH and rigorous interval computations. We also give conditional bounds under explicit global initial zero-strip hypotheses, including $|\operatorname{Im}z|\le3/4$ for the zeros of $H_0^L$.

papers.title: A Hypergeometric RM Surface: Integral Monodromy and Level-11 Covers
papers.abstract: We study the Jacobians of a genus-two family with real multiplication by $K=\Q(\sqrt5)$. We realize these abelian surfaces as factors of cyclic-cover Jacobians and determine their integral rank-two monodromy. For the real embedding with $\sqrt5>0$, the projective image is the Hecke group $\Delta(2,5,\infty)$; the conjugate real image is nondiscrete. After a finite base change, we give an explicit degree-four map from Cohen--Wolfart's Hecke cyclic curve to the genus-two curve. Four deck translates of the induced Jacobian pullback give an integral isomorphism from the fourth power of the surface to the eight-dimensional primitive order-$20$ factor, with an explicit nonproduct polarization. At the primes above $11$, the degree-$12$ torsion-line covers are normalizations of quadratic fibre products of genus-one triangular modular curves. We also describe the associated split and nonsplit Cartan-normalizer covers. Finite-field hypergeometric traces give the local Euler factors and a quadratic transformation with a twist by the quadratic character of $2$.

papers.title: Contiguous relations for elliptic analogues of partial sums of very-well-poised ${}_8\psi_8$ series
papers.abstract: We introduce finite elliptic analogues of partial sums of a balanced very-well-poised ${}_8\psi_8$ series. By combining Abel's lemma on summation by parts with the Riemann theta relation, we establish two contiguous relations. Iterating the second relation gives two finite transformation formulas.

papers.title: Subshifts of finite type and parameter density for intermediate \(-\beta\)-transformations
papers.abstract: We study the subshifts \(\Omega_{-\beta,\alpha}\) associated with the intermediate \(-\beta\)-transformations \(x\mapsto-\beta x+\alpha\pmod1\), where \((\beta,\alpha)\in\Delta_-:=\{(b,a):1<b<2,\ b-1<a<1\}\). We prove that $\Omega_{-\beta,\alpha}$ is of finite type if and only if both endpoints of \([0,1]\) reach the discontinuity \(c_{\beta,\alpha}=\alpha/\beta\). We also prove that the set of parameters \((\beta,\alpha)\) for which \(\Omega_{-\beta,\alpha}\) is a subshift of finite type is dense in \(\Delta_-\). The approximating parameters can be chosen so that both kneading invariants converge to those of the original map.

papers.title: Universal Implications Among $k$-Prime Graph Labelings
papers.abstract: For $k\ge1$, let $\mathcal P_k$ be the class of graphs admitting a bijective labeling by consecutive integers beginning at $k$, with coprime labels at adjacent vertices. We determine all universal inclusions between distinct such classes: $\mathcal P_i\subseteq\mathcal P_j$ holds for $i\ne j$ if and only if $(i,j)=(2,1)$ or $(3,1)$. In particular, the classes are pairwise distinct. The proof translates universal inclusion into a spanning-embedding question for coprimality graphs on consecutive integer intervals. Edge-count identities, arithmetic-progression estimates, and prime-residue switching exclude all other inclusions; a prime-gap argument reduces the remaining finite range to fifteen explicit rational inequalities. We further show that, for each nonexceptional ordered pair, the graph orders at which edge counts obstruct inclusion have a positive natural density. This density is described through a limiting distribution of correlated Euler products, for which we give an atomlessness argument. The classification resolves the distinct-index formulation of the universal-implication conjecture.

papers.title: Parking Functions inspired by board games
papers.abstract: We introduce two new parking schemes inspired by the classic board games Monopoly and backgammon. We consider a one-way street with $n$ parking spots and a queue of $n$ cars waiting to park. Each car has a preferred parking spot and enters in sequence to park. Under the Monopoly parking scheme, if a car finds its preferred spot occupied, it returns to the start of the street and parks in the first available spot it encounters. Under the backgammon parking scheme, if a car finds its preferred spot occupied, it bumps the already parked car out of that spot and takes its place. The bumped car then returns to the start of the street and parks in the first available spot it encounters. A preference list is a parking function for a given parking scheme if all cars successfully park under that scheme. We prove that all preference lists are parking functions under both the Monopoly and backgammon parking schemes. However, the final parking order differs significantly between the two schemes. For a fixed permutation $\pi$, we provide a product formula for the number of Monopoly parking functions resulting in the outcome $\pi$. Analogously, we show that the number of backgammon parking functions with outcome $\pi$ is bounded below by $2^{n-1}$ and bounded above by the $n$-th Catalan number. We also obtain exact formulas involving Motzkin numbers for several families of outcomes. We define the displacement of a car as the absolute difference between the spot where a car ultimately parks and its preferred spot. Displacement multisets encode the displacements for cars with nonzero displacement. We provide formulas for the number of backgammon parking functions with a fixed displacement multiset of cardinality at most $2$, as well as for the number of Monopoly parking functions whose displacement multiset is a given singleton set. We conclude with some directions for further research.
